title: Accounts
description: Real bank-account balances, hand-read off the bank at the end of a month. Not bookkeeping: there are no transactions here, just "this is what was actually in the account when the month closed". A balance read at the end of month M opens month M+1's rolling budget, and from there it is carried forward month by month, so it genuinely depletes. Months at or before M ignore it entirely — a past balance isn't known and isn't guessed. Both pots are modelled, and each rolls forward by its own arithmetic: a private balance by opening + net income - private expenses, a company balance by opening + company income - company expenses - employer social - gross salary. The company one used to be left out, on the grounds that company money is spent down rather than accumulated — that only held while every month drew a full salary, which empties it by construction. A month at the statutory minimum or on a fixed salary leaves money behind, so the company is a balance that carries like any other. Hand-edited and committed via git.

kind.description: Which pot the money is in, spelled the same way budget.json's groups spell it. company: the money the company holds. It enters the ledger straight after Company income and before the employer-social/gross-salary/employee-social/income-tax cascade, so it raises what a full salary can afford — and a negative one lowers it. What the cascade leaves behind is the next month's opening. private: money already drawn. It opens the rolling budget under Net income, as it always has, and is spent down by private expenses. Every account must declare one explicitly; there is no default, because guessing wrong moves real money from one side of the payroll cascade to the other.

balance.description: Euros, decimals allowed (e.g. 1427.42). May be negative for an overdrawn account.

as_of.description: The month-end date this balance was read, e.g. "2026-07-31". It is the CLOSING balance of that month, so it becomes the OPENING balance of the next one: a balance dated 2026-07-31 is August's starting figure and has no effect on July. Only the month matters; the day is informational. Accounts are summed per kind, but both sums are anchored at the single latest as_of among all of them, so read every account together — one stale entry silently drags the whole figure, whichever pot it is in.

note.description: Free-text context, shown next to the account name. Not used in any computation.
